title: 1st Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The first sitting of the third session opened at 09:01 with routine business: earlier minutes were accepted and committee seat changes were announced. The Majlis then voted 57-0 to debate an urgent motion from MDP's Kendhoo MP on Israel blocking the Global Sumud Flotilla carrying aid to Gaza, which includes Maldivians. Thirteen members spoke in the one-hour debate, with PNC and MDP members agreeing on the humanitarian cause but trading criticism over politics and past policy towards Israel; no decision beyond allowing the debate is recorded. The President's five nominations were sent to committees, two items were read for the first time, and after a recess debate began on the government's Re-employment Bill, which lets civil servants work up to age 75, and continues into the next part. The part opens mid-speech in the debate on the Employment Bill, a speaker backing the bill and arguing that people over 65 should be allowed to keep working. The chair then adjourned that debate to next Monday and moved to the resolution from Madaveli MP Mohamed Shameez asking for fast action on corruption flagged in the Auditor General's special audit of Fenaka Corporation. Ten members spoke on it, all in favour of an investigation and tough action, and many also traded blame over the MDP and earlier governments. No vote was taken in this part and the debate carries on into the next one. The text layer is garbled in places, so some details are approximate. This short closing part carries the end of a member's speech that began in the previous part (the speaker's name and the agenda item are not in this part's text). The member spoke about corruption and theft of public money, calling for stronger internal and national audit, laws that stop offenders from escaping, and quicker justice, and also traded criticism with the MDP and the PPM-era government over past corruption. The chair then ended the day's debate, with no vote in this part, and set the next sitting for Monday 6 October 2025 at 09:00. The text layer is garbled in places and the chair is not named, so some wording is inferred.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said Palestine has long had Maldivian support and criticised the motion as politically driven, citing MDP's record while in government.
Raised a point of order that Israeli nationals are barred from entering on Israeli passports and that any other entry should be reported to authorities.
Backed the resolution and said the audit shows large-scale corruption under the MDP-era government.
Criticised MDP leaders for calling a rally over alleged looting while the audit findings emerged under their government.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the government and the President have spoken most on Palestine abroad, and questioned why the proposers had not held a protest.
Was cut off by the chair when his time ran out on the motion.
On the Re-employment Bill, backed letting experienced state staff work to 75 given an ageing population and falling birth rate.
Cited audit findings of large losses, accounts misreported, and agreements given to associates without bidding.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Presented the urgent motion asking the Majlis to bring Israeli obstruction of the flotilla, which includes Maldivian nationals, to the government's attention.
Thanked members for accepting the debate and urged the government to engage with the flotilla and protect Maldivians aboard.
Raised a point of order that the debate was being turned into politics; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Backed the Re-employment Bill as vital for a growing older population and asked for quick committee passage.
Spoke on the flotilla and corrected a claim about how many Maldivians took part; the chair redirected him to the bill.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Backed the bill as fulfilling a presidential pledge, citing pension savings, labour shortages in the atolls and Singapore's 2022 law.
Gave a timeline of how the Fenaka case was raised and shelved, and said the audit should not be dismissed as political.
Said contracts were split to avoid procurement rules and urged the Finance Committee to study the report quickly.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Backed the motion, noted about 66,000 Palestinians killed, and criticised Arab states for inaction.
Supported the resolution and said past MPs also had a role; he had submitted evidence earlier without follow-up.
Called for a careful, fair investigation, punishment of offenders, and recovery of the money.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the motion was important and not political, but that Israeli military personnel reportedly still holiday in Maldives.
Said dual-passport holders could still enter despite the Israeli passport ban.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Condemned Israel's actions, said US backing enables them, and suggested boycotting Israeli- and US-linked goods.
Compared national debt across past governments and said corruption has persisted over 17 years.
Proposed legal changes so officials face criminal charges and cannot trade through state companies.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Asked why MDP never issued a formal English statement condemning Israel, and cited its 2008-era agreements with Israel.
Repeated the accusation before the chair interrupted as the debate hour ended.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said Palestinians' rights have been denied for decades and urged all members to back more action by Maldives and Muslim countries.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Thanked the proposer, said Maldives has spoken for Palestine at every forum, and questioned politicising the matter.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Thanked the proposer and PNC members for accepting the debate, said no government could act otherwise, and wished the Maldivian participant success.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Condemned the attack on the flotilla, called for cross-party action, and asked why earlier governments had not banned Israeli passports.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Argued the motion was politically motivated, said the Foreign Ministry is monitoring the flotilla, and recalled earlier MDP-era contacts with Israel.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Raised a point of order to respond that MDP had issued English statements; the chair declined to take it as the debate had ended.

speakers.name: Hanan Mohamed Rasheed
positions: Presented the Re-employment Bill: state employees could work to age 75, with set criteria, to keep senior expertise and pass knowledge to younger staff.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Introduced the resolution: the audit shows work worth over MVR 2 billion given out outside normal procedures, so institutions should investigate and act faster.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported the resolution and said corruption cases should not be politicised.
Called for a fair investigation and trial, and asked about other unresolved cases.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the resolution and described the Fenaka losses as among the largest from a state company.
Said earlier anti-corruption reports were not acted on and called for the strongest penalties.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Backed the resolution and criticised the MDP's planned rally over alleged looting.
Supported the President's anti-corruption work.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the resolution and recalled the 2018 change of government over corruption.
Argued the audit shows large sums lost; speech continues into the next part.

decisions: Minutes of the 23rd to 27th sittings of the second session were accepted without amendment.
The Majlis voted 57-0 to allow debate on the urgent motion on the Global Sumud Flotilla; debate ran to the one-hour limit.
Non-resident ambassador nominations were sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
National Integrity Commission nominees were sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominees were sent to the Judiciary Committee.
The ILO Constitution 1986 amendment acceptance was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The Human Rights Commission nominee was sent to the Human Rights and Gender Committee.
A recess ran from 10:29 to 11:01 before the Re-employment Bill debate began.
The chair adjourned debate on the Employment Bill (item 8.1) to next Monday.
The chair set 4 hours of total debate time for the Fenaka audit resolution, split by party.
The sitting broke at 12:00 and resumed at 13:01; no vote was held on the resolution in this part.
The chair ended the day's debate; the next sitting was set for Monday 6 October 2025 at 09:00.
